ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
On an insulated smooth horizontal table, there are two stationary small balls A and B, with B at the edge of the table. Both A and B can be considered as point masses, each with a mass of $m = 0.2\mathrm{kg}$. Ball A carries a positive charge with a charge amount of $q = 0.1\mathrm{C}$. Ball B is an insulator and carries no charge. The height of the table above the ground is $h = 0.05\mathrm{m}$. Initially, A and B are separated by a distance of $L = 0.1\mathrm{m}$. Under the influence of a uniform electric field with a horizontal rightward direction and a magnitude of $E = 10\mathrm{N/C}$, ball A begins to move to the right and collides with ball B. During the collision, the total energy of A and B is conserved without any loss, and there is no charge transfer between A and B. Take $g = 10\mathrm{m/s^2}$.

1. After how long will A collide with B?
2. What is the horizontal distance between the landing points of A and B?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, on the left side of a smooth horizontal tabletop there is a small ball A, and at the right table edge there is a small ball B; the horizontal distance between A and B is labeled L. The height from the tabletop to the ground is labeled h. Multiple horizontal arrows in the figure all point to the right, indicating that the direction of the uniform electric field is to the right. Then reason: A is positively charged, and in the rightward uniform electric field it is subjected to a horizontal electric field force F=qE=0.1×10=1 N. The acceleration of A is a=F/m=qE/m=1/0.2=5 m/s^2. A starts from rest and hits B after moving distance L=0.1 m, so L=(1/2)at^2, that is, 0.1=(1/2)×5×t^2, giving t^2=0.04, t=0.2 s. The speed of A before collision is v=at=5×0.2=1 m/s. The collision is a one-dimensional elastic collision, and the two balls have equal masses while B is initially at rest, so after the collision A stops, and B obtains a speed of 1 m/s and leaves the table edge to the right. The falling time T=sqrt(2h/g)=sqrt(2×0.05/10)=sqrt(0.01)=0.1 s. B is uncharged and flies out horizontally at uniform speed, with horizontal displacement x_B=vT=1×0.1=0.1 m. After collision, A has horizontal initial speed 0 at the table edge, but it is still subjected to the rightward electric field force, and its acceleration is 5 m/s^2; during falling, its horizontal displacement is x_A=(1/2)aT^2=(1/2)×5×(0.1)^2=0.025 m. The horizontal distance between the two landing points is |x_B-x_A|=0.1-0.025=0.075 m.
